notes: Both backends now skip symlinks unless --links is set and log a notice naming the flag; with --links they are exposed as `<name>.rclonelink`. In zip the member body already is the target, and in squashfs it is served from LinkTarget with range clamping, and List and NewObject agree on names. Gaps: the hostile-archive protection relies entirely on the local backend, and its test is weak because `outside` never exists, so it would pass even without any protection.

Implements the --links convention in both backends: zip and squashfs symlinks get the .rclonelink suffix, the skip notice names the flag, squashfs Open honours range/seek, and List and NewObject apply the same naming. However, the escape protection relies entirely on the local backend, and the escape test only covers a target that does not exist, so a symlink to an existing directory written before its member is not shown to be safe.
